rationale: The agent authenticated the user via email lookup and retrieved user/order details, which aligns with policy. However, several policy-critical issues occurred: (1) There is no evidence the agent obtained explicit user confirmation before executing any order-changing writes (returns, item modification, address change), which the policy requires. (2) The user wanted to return a bookshelf and a jigsaw from different orders; the agent initiated a single return for two item IDs under order #W6239298 and never executed a return on #W8660475, despite fetching its details—suggesting one of the two intended returns was not performed and/or was applied to the wrong order. (3) The agent modified the pending order item first, then attempted to change the shipping address, which the system disallows post-modification; this led to a handoff. This indicates improper sequencing and incomplete fulfillment of the address-change request. (4) It attempted an address update with a specific address rather than clearly using the user’s default profile address, and then stated a need for human help because the user cannot reveal the address—internally inconsistent. (5) The requested tracking number for the cancelled order was not provided; there is no tool call or final information supplying it. Given missing confirmations, incomplete/possibly incorrect returns, failed address change, and lack of the requested tracking info, the conversation does not meet the pass bar.
